chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'The Satan is most troublesome with the human being when he is alone, isolated. I (peace be upon him) should not see him sleeping alone.'
ai.seo_question: Why is it recommended to avoid sleeping alone according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies solitude as the peak moment for Satan's whispering, linking physical isolation to heightened spiritual vulnerability. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on 'muraqabah' (awareness of God) and suggests that maintaining a state of alertness or companionship mitigates the ease with which Shaytan exploits the quiet mind. The prohibition against sleeping alone serves as a practical safeguard against the 'waswasa' (intrusive thoughts) that arise when one is unguarded.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Satan<sup>la</sup> is the most troublesome with the human being when he happens to be alone, isolated. I<sup>asws</sup> should not see him sleeping alone’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban al-Ahmar from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
has said that Satan is the strongest against man when he is alone without anything and I say that he must not sleep alone.’”
